newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Moody's warns on Australian redraw loans.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Moody's warns on Australian redraw loans.

text.p: Investors in Australia's mortgage-backed securities market may be feeling the effects of intense competition between home lenders, and in the case of redraw loans, the effects may be adverse, Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday.

In a special report, Moody's said the typical redraw loan allows borrowers to make surplus principal payments during the life of the loan, with the ability to subsequently redraw cash back up to the scheduled amortising loan balance.

"Redraw loans may cause dilution in the amount of credit support if the structure does not allow for the level of credit support to be adjusted proportionately to the increase in pool balance as a result of borrowers' exercising their redraw options," Moody's said.
Also, the redraw loan could potentially increase the prepayment volatility of mortgaged-backed securities.

As the Australian mortgage-based securities market evolves, and competition in the lending market intensifies, Moody's sai it expects new mortgage loan products to be made available to potential borrowers.
"The introduction of the redraw loan is an example of how the current lending environment can affect the expectations of mortgage-backed securities investors," Moody's said.

Moody's said it will analyse a new product's impact on a mortgage-backed securitisation transaction when it comes to the market. If it could lead to an increased level of risk, as with the redraw loan, the credit rating agency said it will examine the structure for factors which may offset the risk.
"If an issuer properly addresses these risks, securities will still be eligible for Moody's highest ratings," it added.
